branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Internal process intensifies, official access narrows, or external reporting shifts from existence of complaint to specific verified allegations.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Investigation deepens, leadership prepares contingency actions, and public scrutiny rises if verification or leaks occur.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Preliminary assessment finds credible evidence or corroborating records supporting material allegations.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Reduction in institutional activity, absence of further sourcing momentum, or formal closure language if disclosure rules permit.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Matter is closed or narrowed, but lingering suspicion may remain if public awareness preceded explanation.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Preliminary review finds the complaint unsupported, procedurally defective, or too weak to pursue.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Public reports include nonpublic specifics unavailable from official statements.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Media narrative outruns formal process, trust fractures inside the agency, and leadership shifts into containment mode.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: A staff member or adjacent insider shares complaint details or investigative fragments outside approved channels.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Public or internal discussion shifts from individual guilt to process redesign, audit, or rule changes.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: Actors separate the individual case from system issues and launch policy review, training, or disclosure-rule adjustments.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Handling tensions reveal gaps in procurement oversight, confidentiality practice, or complaint processing regardless of allegation merits.

branch_hypotheses.observable_divergence_signal: Repeated references to an unresolved complaint with little new evidence and declining public attention.
branch_hypotheses.plausible_path: A low-grade legitimacy cloud persists without decisive outcome, producing rumor cycles and fatigue.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Complaint remains unresolved while confidentiality rules keep facts obscured and reporters cannot fully verify.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Official denial and unknown complaint content prevent strong prior confidence.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal outcome in which the complaint results in an official substantiated finding or equivalent confirmed misconduct determination regarding the procurement official.
endpoint_ledger.label: Substantiated wrongdoing finding

meta.important_question: Will the complaint against the procurement official be substantiated by later verified findings?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Substantiation is a core branch explicitly implied by scenario focus.
realization_criteria: A formal ethics finding, disciplinary notice, investigative report, or authoritative city action explicitly states the official committed misconduct or violated rules.
The finding is attributable to a recognized authority actor rather than rumor or anonymous reporting.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: A complaint exists, but no determination is available at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Public suspicion may persist even if the case closes, so narrative closure may differ from procedural closure.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal outcome in which the complaint is dismissed, closed, or otherwise resolved without a substantiated misconduct finding.
endpoint_ledger.label: Case closed without substantiation

meta.important_question: Will the matter be dismissed, closed, or otherwise end without a substantiated wrongdoing finding?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly includes dismissal as a central alternative endpoint.
realization_criteria: A formal closure, declination, dismissal, or equivalent official record indicates no substantiated wrongdoing finding will issue from this complaint.
No later authoritative reversal reopens the same matter within the observed horizon.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Dismissal/closure is explicitly named as a branch, but no early merits assessment is known.

blockers: fear of retaliation or source exposure
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A leak can coexist with either substantiation or dismissal; it is terminal here as a distinct public-state endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal outcome in which significant nonpublic details from the complaint or inquiry enter public circulation through leaks or unauthorized disclosure.
endpoint_ledger.label: Material leak of nonpublic details

meta.important_question: Will nonpublic complaint details or investigative information leak into media or public circulation?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Leak risk is one of the scenario's stated central uncertainties.
realization_criteria: Media reports, public documents, or acknowledged disclosures reveal specific nonpublic complaint contents, evidence, or internal investigative steps not previously officially released.
The revealed details are substantial enough to alter public understanding of the case.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Staff fear leaks and journalists already have partial awareness, creating a credible leak pathway at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Reform can occur whether or not the official is ultimately cleared or sanctioned.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal outcome in which the city implements concrete reforms to procurement oversight, complaint handling, confidentiality practice, or related governance procedures tied to this episode.
endpoint_ledger.label: Procedural reform adopted

meta.important_question: Will the city adopt concrete procedural reforms tied to the complaint or its handling?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly asks for branches around procedural reform.
realization_criteria: A formally adopted policy change, audit implementation, training mandate, structural review, or rules revision is announced or enacted and explicitly linked to the complaint or its handling.
The action goes beyond temporary messaging or an informal promise to review.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Procedural reform is an explicit branch but depends on system-level learning or pressure not yet evidenced.

The exact decision rights between ethics office, leadership, and other oversight bodies are not fully specified in the source text.
The official may suffer reputational damage even without substantiation because complaint existence is already partially known.
General public attention may remain limited unless journalists obtain specifics or leaders mishandle messaging.

simulation_brief.summary: A fictional city ethics office has received a confidential complaint concerning a procurement official. Journalists are aware a complaint exists but do not know its contents. Agency staff are worried about leaks. The official denies wrongdoing. Oversight and confidentiality rules constrain disclosure. T0 should preserve uncertainty over whether allegations are substantiated, dismissed, leaked, or lead to procedural reform.
simulation_brief.t0_posture: early institutional uncertainty with confidentiality pressure and reputational risk

sociology_baseline.note: Actors are likely to update beliefs mainly from moderately credible institutional or media cues, not extreme claims.
Broader public mobilization likely requires concrete details, corroboration, or visible leadership failure.
Confidentiality norms and fear of isolation suppress open internal expression despite private speculation.
Institutional actors cluster with process-oriented peers while media cluster around accountability frames.
Calls for procedural reform likely need reinforcement from multiple elites, reports, or documented process gaps.
Role-based identity as staff, investigators, officials, or journalists shapes interpretation of proper conduct.
Without new verified developments, public attention may fade or remain localized.
